# YM11: 茹古涵今 Rugu Hanjin, "Seize the Old; It Contains the Present"

Malone calls it Ju Ku Han Chin.

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM11` · Page: `/scenes/#YM11` · Row: `research/buildings/YM11-rugu-hanjin/`

## What it was

茹古涵今 Rugu Hanjin, a library court north of 长春仙馆 and south of 坦坦荡荡 (S05 j81:3b, 4b): the five-bay hall 茹古涵今 facing south, behind it the square hall 韶景轩 Shaojing Xuan of five bays on each face, 茂育斋 Maoyu Zhai east and 竹香斋 Zhuxiang Zhai west in front of it, and 静通斋 Jingtong Zhai to the north (S05 j81:3b). 韶景轩 carried a plaque on each of its four eaves: 喜接南薰 south, 景丽东皇 east, 翠生西岭 west, 清风北户 north (S05 j81:4a). Malone calls its roof double (S02 p.80, in the halls table). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S42, S01).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Preface of 1744: "繚以曲垣綴以周廊邃館明忩牙籖萬軸" (S05 j81:4b): walled by winding walls and strung with galleries, deep halls and bright windows, ten thousand book-scrolls; the poem quotes Du Fu, 'not slighting the moderns, loving the ancients'.
